```{r knitr_setup, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, echo=FALSE}
repo_dir = "/Users/haya1/Documents/LanguageModel_Labels/congressional_bills_v2"
data_dir = file.path(repo_dir, "Data") 
fig_dir = file.path(repo_dir, "Figures and Tables/4.3_lhs_results/")
dir.create(fig_dir, showWarnings=FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

knitr_default_plot <- knitr::knit_hooks$get("plot")  
knitr::knit_hooks$set(plot = function(x, options) {  
  x <- knitr_default_plot(x, options) 
  if(!is.null(options$fig.note)) {  
    x  <- gsub(
      "\\end{figure}", 
      sprintf("\\floatfoot*{Note: %s}\\end{figure}", options$fig.note), 
      x, fixed=T)  
  }
  return(x)
})
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = repo_dir)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  warning=FALSE, 
  message=FALSE, 
  echo = FALSE, 
  dev = "jpeg", 
  dpi=300, 
  fig.path = fig_dir,
  out.height = "\\textheight",  
  out.width = "\\textwidth",
  out.extra = "keepaspectratio=true"
  )

require(dplyr)
require(ggplot2)
require(latex2exp)
require(kableExtra)
require(extrafont)
require(lemon)
source(file.path(repo_dir, "Code/ggplot_theme.r"))
```

# Proxy on the LHS

```{r data_10k}
# Note: prompts were sorted based on the coefficients values of GPT3.5 model.
V.levels <- c("Democrat", "Senate", "DW1")

model.levels <- c("star", "gpt-3.5-turbo-0125", "gpt-4o-2024-05-13")
model.labels <- c("Human", "GPT-3.5", "GPT-4o")

Y.labeller <- function(Y) TeX(sprintf("$Y_{%s}$", Y)) 

prompt_index <- read.csv(file.path(data_dir, "lhs_10k_llm.csv")) %>%
  filter(tolower(model)=="gpt-3.5-turbo-0125") %>%
  group_by(V, Y, coef_name) %>%
  arrange(V, Y, coef_name, coef) %>% mutate(prompt.ordered_coef = row_number()) %>% # create prompt index ordered by coef
  arrange(V, Y, coef_name, t) %>% mutate(prompt.ordered_t = row_number()) %>% # create prompt index ordered by t scores
  ungroup() %>%
  select(V, Y, coef_name, prompt, prompt.ordered_coef, prompt.ordered_t) %>%
  distinct()

regressions.llm <- read.csv(file.path(data_dir, "lhs_10k_llm.csv")) %>%
  merge(x=., y=prompt_index, all=TRUE, sort=FALSE) %>%
  mutate(
    prompt.ordered_coef = as.factor(prompt.ordered_coef),
    prompt.ordered_t = as.factor(prompt.ordered_t),
    model = factor(model, levels=model.levels, labels=model.labels),
    V = factor(V, levels=V.levels)
    ) %>%
  filter(coef_name!="(Intercept)")

regressions.human <- read.csv(file.path(data_dir, "lhs_10k_human.csv")) %>%
  mutate(
    model = "star",
    model = factor(model, levels=model.levels, labels=model.labels),
    V = factor(V, levels=V.levels)
    ) %>%
  filter(coef_name!="(Intercept)")
```

```{r fig01_coef, fig.height=5.5, fig.width=9, fig.cap="$\\beta_1$ vs. Prompt. Proxy on the LHS.", fig.align="center", fig.note="The coefficients were obtained by fitting the model $Y_t = \\beta_{0} + \\beta_{1} V$ over 10,000 bills, with 95\\% confidence intervals computed using robust standard errors. Here, $Y_t$ denotes the indicator for topic $t$, where $Y_t = 1\\{Y = t\\}$ for $t \\in \\mathcal{T}$ and $Y_\\text{Other} = 1\\{Y \\notin \\mathcal{T}\\}$, with $\\mathcal{T} = \\{3, 14, 15, 19, 20\\}$ is the 5 most-common human-labeled topics in the bills data. The variable $V$ takes one of the following bills variables: Democrat, Senate, or DW1, where $\text{Democrat} = 1\\{\\text{Party} = \\text{Democrat}\\}$, $\\text{Senate} = 1\\{\\text{Chamber} = \\text{Senate}\\}$, and DW1 is the imputed DW1 score for the bill sponsor. The regressions based on human-labeled topics (red) were estimated with $Y_{t}^\\text{Human} = 1\\{Y^\\text{Human} = t\\}$, while the LLM-based regressions (GPT-3.5 in green, circles; and GPT-4o in blue, triangles) were estimated with $Y_{t,m,p}^\\text{LLM} = 1\\{Y_{m,p}^\\text{LLM} = t\\}$, where $m \\in \\{\\text{GPT-3.5}, \\text{GPT-4o}\\}$ denotes the LLM model and $p \\in \\{1, \\ldots, 12\\}$ denotes the prompt modifications. In each subplot, the indices for the prompts reflect the order chosen based on sorting the estimated values of the GPT-3.5 model in ascending order. The corresponding estimates for GPT-4o are aligned according to this order."}
coefs <- regressions.llm %>%
  ggplot(aes(x=prompt.ordered_coef, color=model, shape=model)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept=0, color=my_palette[["black"]], linewidth=0.2) +

  geom_hline(aes(yintercept=lci, color=model), linetype="dashed", linewidth=0.3, data=regressions.human) +
  geom_hline(aes(yintercept=uci, color=model), linetype="dashed", linewidth=0.3, data=regressions.human) +
  geom_hline(aes(yintercept=coef, color=model), linewidth=0.5, data=regressions.human) +

  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin=lci, ymax=uci), position=position_dodge(width=0.5), width=0.5, linewidth=0.3) +
  geom_point(aes(y=coef), size=1.25, alpha=0.7, position=position_dodge(width=0.5)) +
  
  facet_grid(V ~ Y, labeller=labeller(Y=Y.labeller, .default = label_parsed)) +
  
  xlab("Prompt Index") +
  ylab("Coefficients") +
  
  scale_color_manual(name=NULL, values=my_colors, labels=model.labels) +
  guides(color = guide_legend(override.aes = list(shape = c(NA, 16, 17))),
         shape = "none") +  # merge color and shape legends
  theme.point

coefs
```

```{r fig02_tscore, fig.height=5.5, fig.width=9, fig.cap="t-scores of $\\beta_1$ vs. Prompt. Proxy on the LHS.", fig.align="center", fig.note="The t-scores were obtained by fitting the model $Y_t = \\beta_{0} + \\beta_{1} V$ over 10,000 bills, with 95\\% confidence intervals computed using robust standard errors. Here, $Y_t$ denotes the indicator for topic $t$, where $Y_t = 1\\{Y = t\\}$ for $t \\in \\mathcal{T}$ and $Y_\\text{Other} = 1\\{Y \\notin \\mathcal{T}\\}$, with $\\mathcal{T} = \\{3, 14, 15, 19, 20\\}$ is the 5 most-common human-labeled topics in the bills data. The variable $V$ takes one of the following bills variables: Democrat, Senate, or DW1, where $\text{Democrat} = 1\\{\\text{Party} = \\text{Democrat}\\}$, $\\text{Senate} = 1\\{\\text{Chamber} = \\text{Senate}\\}$, and DW1 is the imputed DW1 score for the bill sponsor. The regressions based on human-labeled topics (red) were estimated with $Y_{t}^\\text{Human} = 1\\{Y^\\text{Human} = t\\}$, while the LLM-based regressions (GPT-3.5 in green, circles; and GPT-4o in blue, triangles) were estimated with $Y_{t,m,p}^\\text{LLM} = 1\\{Y_{m,p}^\\text{LLM} = t\\}$, where $m \\in \\{\\text{GPT-3.5}, \\text{GPT-4o}\\}$ denotes the LLM model and $p \\in \\{1, \\ldots, 12\\}$ denotes the prompt modifications. In each subplot, the indices for the prompts reflect the order chosen based on sorting the estimated values of the GPT-3.5 model in ascending order. The corresponding estimates for GPT-4o are aligned according to this order."}

tscores <- regressions.llm %>%
  ggplot(aes(x=prompt.ordered_t, color=model, shape=model)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept=0, color=my_palette[["black"]], linewidth=0.2) +

  # geom_hline(aes(yintercept=t, color=model), linewidth=0.5, data=regressions.human) +
  geom_point(aes(y=t), size=1.25, alpha=0.7, position=position_dodge(width=0.5)) +

  facet_grid(V ~ Y, labeller=labeller(Y=Y.labeller, .default = label_parsed)) +
  
  xlab("Prompt Index") +
  ylab("t-scores") +

  scale_color_manual(name=NULL, values=my_colors, labels=model.labels[2:3]) +
  guides(color = guide_legend(override.aes = list(shape = c(NA,16, 17)[2:3])),
         shape = "none") +  # merge color and shape legends
  
  theme.point

tscores
```

```{r data_regressions.averaged}
regression.levels <- c("5k_Yllm_V", "train_Yhuman_V", "Ytilde_V")
regression.labels <- c("LLM", "Human Validation", "Debiased")

regressions.averaged <- read.csv(file.path(data_dir, "lhs_5k_llm_human_debiased_averaged.csv")) %>%
  filter(coef_name!="(Intercept)") %>% # Plot only beta_1
  # filter(regressions=="5k_Yllm_V") %>%
   mutate(
     bias_norm = bias_mean/coef_sd, 
     V = factor(V, levels=V.levels),
     model = factor(model, levels=model.levels, labels=model.labels),
     regression = factor(regression, levels=regression.levels, labels=regression.labels)
     ) %>%
  rename(proportion=train_proportion) 

facet.labeller <- labeller(proportion = function(proportion) sprintf("Validation Proportion = %s%%", as.numeric(proportion)*100))

n_bins <- 30
```

```{r fig03_bias1, fig.height=3, fig.width=8, fig.cap="Bias Density of $\\beta_1^\\text{LLM}$ by Proportion of Validation Samples. Proxy on the LHS.", fig.align="center", fig.note="The bias estimates were computed as the difference between the coefficient estimates from $N = 1000$ simulation runs, $\\bar{\\beta}_{t, V, \\eta, m,p} = \\sum_{i=1}^N \\beta_{t, V, \\eta, m,p}^{(i)} / N$, and the human-based coefficient from the entire set of 10,000 bills,  $\\beta_{t,V}^\\star$, using a regression model of the form $Y_t = \\beta_{0} + \\beta_{1} V$, for topic $t\\in\\{3, 14, 15, 19, 20, \\text{Other}\\}$, variable $V\\in\\{\\text{Democrat}, \\text{Senate}, \\text{DW1}\\}$, validation proportion $\\eta\\in\\{5\\%, 10\\%, 25\\%, 50\\%\\}$, LLM model $m \\in \\{\\text{GPT-3.5}, \\text{GPT-4o}\\}$, and prompt $p \\in \\{1, \\ldots, 12\\}$. A random sample of 5,000 bills drawn from the original 10,000 was used, with LLM-based labels, $Y_{t,m,p}^\\text{LLM} = 1\\{Y_{m,p}^\\text{LLM} = t\\}$."}

bias1 <- regressions.averaged %>%
  filter(proportion!=0.25) %>%
  filter(regression=="LLM") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x=bias_mean, y=after_stat(max(group)*count/tapply(count, PANEL, FUN=sum)[PANEL]),
             group=regression, fill=regression)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept=0, color=my_palette[["black"]], linewidth=0.2) +
  geom_histogram(bins=n_bins, color="white") +  
  geom_hline(yintercept=0, color=my_palette[["lightgray"]], linewidth=0.3) +
  facet_grid(. ~ proportion, labeller=facet.labeller) +
  
  xlab("Bias") +
  ylab("Probability Densities") +
  
  scale_fill_manual(name=NULL, values=my_colors) +
  scale_x_symmetric(mid=0) +
  scale_y_continuous(minor_breaks=seq(0,1, by=0.05), limits=c(0,0.25)) +
  theme.bar + 
  guides(fill="none")


bias1
```

```{r fig04_bias1_norm, fig.height=3, fig.width=8, fig.cap="Normalized Bias Density of $\\beta_1^\\text{LLM}$ by Proportion of Validation Samples. Proxy on the LHS.", fig.align="center", fig.note="The normalized bias estimates were computed as the normalized difference between the coefficient estimates from $N = 1000$ simulation runs, $\\bar{\\beta}_{t, V, \\eta, m,p}$, and the human-based coefficient from the entire set of 10,000 bills,  $\\beta_{t,V}^\\star$, divided by the sample standard deviation, $s_{t,V,\\eta, m,p}$, where $s^2_{t,V,\\eta, m,p} = \\sum_{i=1}^N (\\beta_{t,V, \\eta, m,p}^{(i)} - \\bar{\\beta}_{t,V, \\eta, m,p})^2/(N-1)$ and all variables are as defined previously."}

bias1_norm <- regressions.averaged %>%
  filter(proportion!=0.25) %>%
  filter(regression=="LLM") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x=bias_norm, 
             y=after_stat(max(group)*count/tapply(count, PANEL, FUN=sum)[PANEL]),
             group=regression, fill=regression)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept=0, color=my_palette[["black"]], linewidth=0.2) +
  geom_histogram(bins=n_bins, color="white") +
  geom_hline(yintercept=0, color=my_palette[["lightgray"]], linewidth=0.3) +
  facet_grid(. ~ proportion, labeller=facet.labeller) +
  
  xlab("Normalized Bias") +
  ylab("Probability Densities") + 
  
  scale_fill_manual(name=NULL, values=my_colors) +
  scale_x_symmetric(mid=0) +
  scale_y_continuous(minor_breaks=seq(0,1, by=0.05), limits=c(0,0.25)) +
  theme.bar + 
  guides(fill="none")

bias1_norm
```

```{r tab_data}
proportion.levels <- c(0.05, 0.10, 0.25, 0.50)
regressions.averaged$proportion <- factor(
  regressions.averaged$proportion, 
  levels=proportion.levels, 
  labels=sprintf("%s\\%%", proportion.levels*100))

alpha <- 0.10
probs <- c(alpha/2, 1-alpha/2)

stripe <- function(nstriped=3, nrow=50){
  start_row <- rep(seq(0, (2*nstriped)*nrow, by=2*nstriped), each=nstriped)
  return(start_row + rep(1:nstriped, times=length(start_row)/nstriped))
}
```

```{r tab_bias1, results='asis'}
bias1 <- regressions.averaged %>%
  mutate(statistic=bias_mean) %>%
  group_by(proportion, regression) %>%
  summarise(
    "Mean" = mean(statistic),
    "SD" = sd(statistic),
    "Median" = median(statistic),
    "5\\%" = quantile(statistic, probs[1]),
    "95\\%" = quantile(statistic, probs[2]),
    .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
  rename(c(
    "Validation Proportion" = proportion, 
    "Bias" = regression)
    )

kbl(bias1, align="rlrrrrr",
    caption="Bias Summary Statistics of $\\beta_1$ by Proportion of Validation Samples. Proxy on the LHS: $Y = \\beta_{0} + \\beta_{1} V$.",
    digits=3, booktabs=T, linesep = "", escape=F) %>%
  kable_styling(latex_options = "striped", stripe_index = stripe(3))
```

    "Validation Proportion" = proportion, 
    "MSE" = regression
    ))
  
kbl(coverage2, align="lrlrrrrr",
    caption="Coverage Summary Statistics by Model and Proportion of Validation Samples for $\\beta_1$. Proxy on the LHS: $Y = \\beta_{0} + \\beta_{1} V$.",
    digits=3, booktabs=T, linesep = "", escape=F) %>%
  kable_styling(latex_options = "striped", stripe_index = stripe(3))
```
